audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer called levels 6, first-item and two-items 'Skill' while the packet levelChart and the content win[] rows both read Naafiri, Naafiri, Azir. Three of seven rows rendered two different answers.
audit.why: 47.2% over 1106 games with a level-6 dive spike: Naafiri owns the lane until Azir's wall and soldier range outscale her, which is the two-item mark, not level 6.
audit.corrected: phases[4] and phases[5] moved to Naafiri and phases[6] to Azir, with the whys for rows 4 and 5 rewritten in the same proposal so no row argues with itself.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes never named a Naafiri ability or a single cooldown. 'Level 6 adds dive insurance' described Azir's R without saying what it answers.
audit.why: Naafiri's spikes are Eviscerate scaling from 11s to 7s and Hounds' Pursuit at 6 (900 range, 110/95/80s, recastable for a shield). Azir's are Nashor's Tooth and Emperor's Divide, which is terrain and therefore the counter to both of her dashes.
audit.corrected: spikes[0..3].text, breakdown.spikes and the level-6 prose rewritten around those numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Emperor's Divide creates terrain, and every tool Naafiri has for reaching Azir — Eviscerate, Hounds' Pursuit and its recast — is a dash. Instead the page repeated an unsourced claim that you should 'stand near minions to body-block the hounds'.
audit.why: Owner R flag: terrain, 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'. Enemy E and R both carry the dash flag. Enemy passive We Are More: packmates attack the targets of her attacks and abilities — they follow her target, so body-blocking is not the mechanic. Cooldown asymmetry is the other half: Eviscerate 11/10/9/8/7s against Shifting Sands 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s, so she gets roughly two entries per escape Azir owns.
audit.corrected: Wall-vs-dash stated explicitly in winCon, dosFull[2], breakdown.late, spikes[3] and the content late text; the body-block claim removed and replaced with the packmate-targeting mechanic; the dash-to-escape cooldown ratio now carries the trading advice.

audit.why: 47.2% over 1106 games matches the TRICKY / 7-10 rating already on the page.
Hounds' Pursuit 110s at rank 1 / 900 range; Eviscerate 11s at rank 1; Shifting Sands 22s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with all three numbers and the dive-per-escape ratio.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization said 'add anti-heal early into his sustain' — wrong pronoun, and the sustain it refers to is Eviscerate fully healing her PACKMATES, not Naafiri herself.
audit.why: Enemy E text: 'dashes and damages enemies in an area around her, recalling her packmates and fully healing them.'
audit.corrected: Pronoun fixed and the clause pointed at the pack. Whether Grievous Wounds reduces the packmate heal is NOT asserted anywhere — the kit does not say.

audit.whatIsWrong: Naafiri addressed as he/his/him across tldr, winCon, enemyWin, tradeGood, tradeBad, loading, breakdown.wave, breakdown.feeding, three dosFull/dontsFull titles and four report entries.
audit.corrected: All corrected in the proposed strings.

edits.before: Naafiri simply closes distance faster than you can create space, and her passive pack of doggos adds extra damage to any all-in — this is one of your hardest lanes pre-6. Play maximally passive, keep minions between you and her, and don't push the wave since a pushed lane invites a free dash-in kill. Ask jungle for early attention if she starts snowballing.
edits.after: Darkin Daggers reach 900 and bleed while you must step to 525 to place sand, and We Are More sends packmates onto whatever she hits — this is one of your hardest lanes pre-6. Play passive, keep the wave on your side, and never be caught with Shifting Sands down: Eviscerate is 11 seconds against your 22. Ask jungle for early attention.

edits.before: Her ultimate adds a long-range leap to her all-in kit, letting her close gaps you thought were safe, so respect her all-in potential even at 6 when your own R comes online. Use R defensively to wall off her dash path rather than trying to trade — you're still the weaker combatant in a direct fight here. Focus on farming safely and avoid dying, since your scaling is what wins this matchup, not early trades.
edits.after: Hounds' Pursuit dashes at you from 900 and recasts for a shield, so level 6 does not make you safe — it makes her longer-ranged. Emperor's Divide is the real answer because it is terrain: hold it for the moment she commits Eviscerate or R and the dive ends against a wall of sand. Farm safely and avoid dying, since scaling wins this, not early trades. Ping every roam — her pack clears waves fast.

edits.before: Once you have your first item you can start punishing her dash cooldowns with poke damage, though she remains a threat if she catches you isolated. By two items your zone control and R wall give you real answers to keep her out of range entirely, and your scaling damage output outclasses her flat snowball-reliant kit. Build early defensive stats (Zhonya's) if she's ahead, since a fed Naafiri can still delete you in one dash-chain. In fights, hold R until she commits her engage, then wall her off from your team.
edits.after: Nashor's Tooth makes soldier autos hurt on her dash downtime, though Eviscerate at 7 seconds still gets her in if you are isolated. By two items Emperor's Divide is the whole answer: it is terrain, and every tool she owns for reaching you — Eviscerate, Hounds' Pursuit, its recast — is a dash. Build Zhonya's if she is ahead, since a fed Naafiri deletes you in one chain. In fights hold R until she commits, then wall her off from your team and let the soldiers grind down the packmates.

notes: Naafiri is female; the shipped page used he/his/him in eleven fields. Packet defect confirmed: not one Naafiri ability was named. Level chart disagreed across layers on rows 4, 5 and 6 (full said Skill three times, content and packet said Naafiri/Naafiri/Azir) — full has been moved to match, with the whys for the two flipped rows rewritten in the same proposal. Removed the unsourced 'stand near minions to body-block the hounds' line: We Are More says packmates attack the targets of her attacks and abilities, i.e. they follow her target, and nothing in the kit supports body-blocking. The anti-heal missing-interaction is real but narrower than the rule implies — Eviscerate fully heals her PACKMATES, not Naafiri, so the page now describes the pack re-heal without claiming Grievous Wounds reduces it. RATING SEMANTICS UNRESOLVED, see questionsForUser: phases[N].rating is 7/10 on Naafiri-winning rows here but 6/10 on Azir-winning rows in azir_mid__mel, so I could not tell whether it means difficulty-for-Azir or Azir-favourability. I left every rating untouched in both files rather than guess.
